findings.evidence: Full read of Tensor.lean: the only equational lemmas about `fromG1G2` are `fromG1G2_apply` (217), `fromG1G2_zero` (224), `_reverse` (254), `_neg` (262), `_inj` (356); `spinStructureTwo_eq` (114) covers only E₂, and `S_⊥` appears nowhere in the code.
findings.fix: Add e.g. `fromG1G2_eq_bilinMap : fromG1G2 ε K g₁ g₂ = (√(K.M2 g) / g K.p K.q) • ε.bilinMap ![K.q, g₁ • K.S + g₂ • (K.S - (g K.S K.q / g K.p K.q) • K.p)]` (with `g K.p K.q ≠ 0` if needed; the junk-value convention may make it unconditional, since both sides carry the factor `M/(p·q)`), and point the docstrings at it.
findings.issue: The `fromG1G2` docstring (lines 209-211) and the module docstring (lines 29-33) state `fromG1G2 ε K g₁ g₂ = (M/(p·q)) · ε(·,·,q, g₁ S + g₂ (S − ((S·q)/(p·q)) p))` as the defining "standard form", but no lemma in the file states it; `fromG1G2_apply` only gives the two-structure sum. A consumer comparing with the literature, or wanting the single-four-form expression, has to redo the algebra, and the advertised characterization is unusable and unchecked.

findings.evidence: BilinMap.lean:97-99 `@[simp] theorem bilinMap_pair_smul_snd`, 138-140 `@[simp] theorem bilinMap_pair_neg_snd`, 157-159 `theorem bilinMap_pair_sub_snd` with no attribute.
findings.fix: Tag `bilinMap_pair_sub_snd` with `@[simp]` (its LHS `f.bilinMap ![a, b - c]` is in normal form, as for the smul and neg versions).
findings.issue: `bilinMap_pair_sub_snd` is not `@[simp]`, while the two parallel pair lemmas are: `bilinMap_pair_smul_snd` (line 97) and `bilinMap_pair_neg_snd` (line 138). So `f.bilinMap ![a, r • b]` and `f.bilinMap ![a, -b]` normalize under `simp` but `f.bilinMap ![a, b - c]` does not, an inconsistent normal form for the same family.

summary: Prior findings are resolved (coefficient uniqueness is now public; the εWit alias is replaced by Matrix.det_fin_four/detRowAlternating_fin_four; the rename leaves no compatibility surface). Remaining: the "standard form" identity that both docstrings advertise for fromG1G2 has no lemma, and one of the three new pair lemmas in BilinMap.lean is missing the @[simp] its siblings carry.
